newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra, News in talks to shorten rollout.
newsitem.headline: Telstra, News in talks to shorten rollout.

text.p: Government-owned telecoms group Telstra Corp is in talks with News Corp Ltd about shortening Telstra's cable rollout for their jointly-owned Foxtel cable television joint venture, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Tuesday.
"Sources said that Telstra chief executive Frank Blount had discussed the issue with senior News executives over the past two days," the newspaper said.
"A roll-out deal could leave Testra with a cable network passing little more than two million homes, rather than the original target of four million," the newspaper said.
"One option for ending the deal would have Testra pay its way out of the deal, possibly at a cost of several hundred million dollars, sources said," the newspaper reported.
The talks are believed to have taken place between retiring News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley and Blount, it said.
The deal under discussion would halve the original A$4 billion cost of the rollout plan but leave Telstra's rollout short of its competitor Optus Communiciation's 2.3 million home rollout.
